projects.summary: Optivision is a comprehensive B2B CRM and ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) solution designed to enable optical stores to manage their customer, prescription, order, financial, and inventory processes end-to-end.
projects.slug: By digitising businesses’ paperwork, it enables them to create prescriptions, track customer accounts and view income and expenditure analyses in a matter of seconds.
projects.title: Optivison
projects.description:
# **Key Features**

Comprehensive Prescription and Order Management: Accurate digital recording and tracking of customers’ eye measurement values (spherical, cylindrical, axis, etc.).

* **Finance and Accounts Receivable Module:** Real-time monitoring of the business’s income-expense balance and customer-based credit/debt records.
* **Telegram Integration:** Automatic delivery of critical notifications and daily summary reports to the business owner’s Telegram account.
* **Advanced Authentication (Auth):** Secure user login and role-based access management using Supabase Auth.
* **Modern and Responsive Interface:** Dark Mode support, “Premium” login animations, and mobile-responsive design.

##  **Technical Architecture and Technologies Used**

This project is built using a scalable, performance-focused architecture that adheres to current industry standards:

### **Frontend Technologies:**

* **React 18 & TypeScript:** A modular architecture enhanced with robust type safety, a goal of zero “runtime errors,” and modern React hooks.
* **Vite:** An ultra-fast bundler preferred over Webpack, offering instant HMR (Hot Module Replacement).
* **State Management:** TanStack Query (React Query) was used for asynchronous data fetching, caching, and optimistic UI updates.
* **UI & CSS:** Tailwind CSS was integrated for a utility-first approach, along with customizable shadcn/ui components (Radix UI) that comply with accessibility (a11y) standards. Form management and validation were handled using React Hook Form + Zod.
* **Data Visualization:** Recharts was used to dynamically plot financial metrics.

### Backend & Database:

**Supabase:** A PostgreSQL-based database infrastructure. Database-level security was ensured through Row Level Security (RLS) rules. Real-time database listening features enabled instant updates.

### Deployment and DevOps Processes

The project has been designed with an isolated architecture to ensure it runs with the same stability across all environments:

* **Docker:** The application has been containerized using a Dockerfile and compiled to run on a lightweight Nginx image (Alpine). This completely eliminates dependency issues.
* **VPS and Reverse Proxy:** The project has been deployed on an Ubuntu-based VPS using Docker Compose. A primary Nginx layer has been positioned as a reverse proxy in front of the server, and incoming HTTP requests are routed to the underlying containers.
* **CI/CD Setup:** The project’s GitHub repository has been prepared for an infrastructure where Docker images will be automatically built via GitHub Actions and pushed to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).



### Highlights:

* **Type Safety:** By using TypeScript interfaces and types throughout the codebase, runtime errors have been prevented and code readability has been improved.
* **Modern State Management:** Instead of cumbersome structures like Redux, TanStack Query was successfully implemented by clearly separating server-state and client-state.
* **Component-Oriented Architecture:** Reusable and isolated React components (Dashboard, Orders, Revenue) compliant with SOLID principles were created under the \`components/\` directory.
* **Real-World Problem Solving:** This project is not just a “To-Do app” clone; it is a working product that solves the complex business logic (prescription math, debt management) of a real-world business in the optical industry.

projects.description:
# Technology Stack

## Frontend

* **Framework & Language:** React 18, TypeScript
* **Bundler:** Vite
* **State & Data Management:** TanStack React Query v5
* **Styling & UI Architecture:** Tailwind CSS, Radix UI
* **Forms & Validation:** React Hook Form and Zod
* **Data Visualization:** Recharts (Interactive charts for dashboards)

## Backend

* **Framework & Language:** Node.js, Express.js, TypeScript
* **Database & ORM:** PostgreSQL 16, Prisma ORM (Robust data modeling and type safety)
* **Authentication:** JWT (JSON Web Token), Bcrypt (Cryptographic encryption)
* **Security & Layers:** Custom Auth Middleware, CORS optimizations

## Architectural Approach

> **TIP**
>
> Why Were TypeScript and Prisma Chosen? TypeScript was chosen for the project to ensure end-to-end type safety. Types automatically generated from database schemas using the Prisma ORM are passed directly to the frontend via the Express API. This approach prevents runtime errors caused by data inconsistencies by 90%.

* Modular and Component-Oriented Architecture: A self-contained, reusable "Shadcn-like" UI architecture was established on the frontend using Radix UI.
* High-Performance Data Management (React Query): React Query was chosen for server state management instead of classic Redux or Context API. This ensures data is automatically cached, fetched in the background, and unnecessary network requests are prevented.
* Relational Database Model: Strong foreign key relationships have been established between Users, Roles, Profiles, Companies, Products, and Quotations within PostgreSQL to ensure data integrity. The system has transitioned to a high-performance ID generation architecture using Postgres’ native gen_random_uuid() function.

## Deployment Process & DevOps

The system runs fully containerized (Dockerized) on an Ubuntu-based VPS.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> The microservices-style Docker architecture project has been deployed using a multi-container architecture to separate dependencies. The frontend, backend, and database are completely isolated from one another but configured to communicate within a closed network.

**1. Docker Multi-Stage Build:**

* **Frontend:** Compiled with Vite in a Node.js container, then the resulting static files are copied to an ultra-lightweight Nginx:Alpine image.
* **Backend:** TypeScript files are compiled (tsc), and the Prisma client is generated (prisma generate). Only the compiled \`dist\` folder and production dependencies are moved to a clean image to optimize image size.

**2. Database Management & Persistence:**

* PostgreSQL version 16 uses a Docker Volume structure to make data persistent against server crashes.
* During initial setup, automatic migration rules such as \`db push --accept-data-loss\` are run via Prisma to instantly synchronize database tables.

**3. Nginx Reverse Proxy & Security:**

* The Nginx on the main server handles incoming HTTP requests.
* It automatically redirects client-side traffic to the Frontend container and traffic with the /api prefix (e.g., /api/auth/register) to the Backend container hidden in the background.
* Dynamic Resolution: To prevent the entire infrastructure from locking up in the event of a container failure, Nginx uses Docker’s internal DNS resolver to perform flexible proxy routing.

**4. CI/CD Infrastructure Compatibility:**

* Thanks to the docker-compose.yml structure in the project, the system works fully integrated with CI/CD tools like GitHub Actions and can be upgraded to new versions in seconds.

projects.summary: JobDetected is an intelligent prediction and classification platform that analyzes the text of job postings on the market (job descriptions, titles, etc.) using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning algorithms.
projects.slug: The primary focus is on seamlessly integrating classic web technologies with Python-based data science models under a single product framework.
projects.title: Job Detected
projects.description:
# Technology Stack

## Client and Web Server Layer

* Core Framework: Node.js (Server) and React (Frontend)
* Containerization: The application’s web layer is fully containerized using Docker (image-based via ghcr.io), ensuring portability and platform independence.
* Security: End-to-end encrypted Session Secret configurations and CORS optimizations are used for user session management.

## Machine Learning and API Layer

* Prediction Engine: Python-based algorithms have been developed for data analysis and model inference.
* Microservice Integration: The Python model is deployed as an independent REST API (microservice) on the PythonAnywhere cloud infrastructure, rather than being embedded within the main Node.js application.
* Communication: Job posting texts received from the client are sent to the Python API via Node.js as asynchronous (Promise/fetch) requests, and the AI’s prediction is displayed on the screen in real time.

## Architectural Approach and Microservice Separation

> **TIP**
>
> Why Were Python and Node.js Separated? Machine learning models consume significant amounts of CPU and memory (RAM). To prevent the Node.js application managing web traffic from slowing down due to AI processing, the "Separation of Concerns" principle was applied. While the web layer runs on a separate VPS (using Docker and Nginx), the CPU-intensive prediction layer is hosted as an isolated service (microservice) on PythonAnywhere.

## Deployment and Nginx Optimizations

* The entire system is managed on an Ubuntu VPS using an Nginx reverse proxy.
* Nginx handles traffic coming to the jobdetected:3000 port, establishing a secure and fast communication channel.
* The Nginx configuration is designed with Dynamic Resolution, providing fault tolerance to prevent other projects (Quote CRM, Optivision, etc.) from being affected in the event of a potential outage in one part of the system.

## Challenges Encountered and Solution Strategies

"Network Latency and Timeout Management," one of the most fundamental challenges of microservice architectures, was encountered in this project and shaped the system’s architectural decisions.

> **NOTE**
>
> Cloud Service Sleep Mode and Timeout Management The project’s forecasting API was deployed on PythonAnywhere for cost optimization purposes. Due to third-party cloud providers’ (PaaS) periodic "Cold Start" (sleep mode) or freezing policies, the API server may occasionally return 404/504 (Gateway Timeout) responses.
>
> This is not a technical coding error but a result of asynchronous wait times in microservice communication between servers. In real-world scenarios (Production), system flexibility has been enhanced by integrating an automatic retry mechanism on the web side or user-friendly "Service Under Maintenance" messages for such "API Unavailable" situations.
